title: ÆTHER: Monsoon Duel (new track 5)
story: Two warriors face each other in monsoon rain. One strike, then the storm breaks.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 16:24: 'lets make 2-3 tracks more'. Fresh mood unlike the four locked tracks (hero intro, dog, villain wedding, car chase): a rain-soaked sword duel. Signature voice: chenda drums and an edakka. Hype rules kept: an attention hit at second 0, a punch hit on every section change, composed wow moments.

positive_global_styles: an epic, hard-hitting sword-duel film score cue in pouring monsoon rain, goosebump-raising, every hit lands like a punch, composed like a senior blockbuster film composer
Kerala chenda drums are the signature voice: thunderous, fast, rolling chenda patterns with huge low taiko hits
an edakka (talking drum) bends its pitch to sing the 4-note warrior hook, answered by bold low brass
thunder used as timpani, rain on metal as hi-hats, sword clashes tuned as metallic percussion hits
big cinematic strings with fast ostinatos, a deep male choir chanting wordless syllables, fresh dark synth bass
loud, clean, wide, very punchy mix with big transients

positive_local_styles: the very first sound, at second zero: one massive attention hit, a thunder crack with a deep sub boom and a chenda slam, then only rain
in the rain, a lone edakka slowly sings the 4-note warrior hook, a low drone underneath, a single sword is drawn with a ringing metallic scrape
transition: a punch hit, then a tense chenda pattern starts and speeds up, the deep choir breathes the hook, strings tremble
transition: a huge sword clash hit, then the full duel groove slams in: thunderous chenda at full speed, low brass blasting the hook, racing string ostinato
tuned sword-clash hits answer each brass phrase
surprise: everything stops dead, only rain and one held low choir note
then three huge slow punch hits, each with a thunder crack, like slow-motion blows

transition: a massive punch hit and the storm breaks: the chenda ensemble and big drums at maximum, the choir shouts the hook, the key lifts up a whole step for the biggest, most hyped hook of the track
the edakka and the brass trade the hook faster and faster
a drum build, then one final massive unison hit with a thunder crack and a deep sub drop
silence, then only rain and the edakka sings the hook one last time, slower, the winner walks away
